messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Multiple GPU OOMs during prefill on gpu-pool-3. 12 container restarts in 5m. Paging @oncall.

oncall: Ack — joining. pulling pod logs now.

maria-sre: seeing repeated stacktrace: `CudaError: out of memory` + immediate container restart. Prefill token counts spike up to ~70k for a few requests.

liam: which model and route?

maria-sre: model=rwd-13b-ctx-v2, route=/v1/generate/stream (router tag: long-context). Originating traffic from customer:datawise-prod.

asha: Support dashboard: Datawise reports streaming truncation + 502s for ~3.2% of requests in last 10m. Increasing error budget burn.

liam: quick triage: likely prefill KV allocation + large seq => LRUs evict and then cudaAlloc fails, triggers restart. Could be kvcache fragmentation.

maria-sre: Mitigation plan (short):
- apply router cap on max_prefill_tokens for route -> 32k
- enable coldmodel fallback for requests > 32k
- temporarily route long-context traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool-b (lower load)
- collect core dumps + upload logs

oncall: I'll apply router cap and enable fallback, then start draining the worst nodes.

liam: command to set cap (running now):
```
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/long-context/actions \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -d '{"action":"set_max_prefill_tokens","value":32768}'
```

maria-sre: `spill_to_disk=true` enabled on runtime config for gpu-pool-3. Restarting pods sequentially to avoid cascades.

oncall: Issued rolling restart for node node-az3-47 (pods: rwd-13b-ctx-v2). Restart in progress.

support-ops: Notifying Datawise; initial message sent: \"We observed GPU memory failures for long-context requests and applied an immediate mitigation (prefill cap + fallback). We'll follow up when stable.\" ETA for next customer update: 15m.

eng-lead: Also add temporary router-side rate limit for requests with content-length > 500k bytes. That will prevent new massive prefill surges while we stabilize.

maria-sre: Logs/artefacts collected: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1859998888/prefill-oom.tar.gz (includes `dmesg`, container logs, nvml traces).

oncall: Observability: prefill_oom_count dropped from 14/min to 2/min after mitigation. Restart rate stabilized. Monitoring for 30m.

liam: Opening incident ticket and assigning postmortem. Immediate follow-ups:
1) investigate kv-cache fragmentation and consider opportunistic compaction
2) evaluate lowering default max_prefill_tokens for public router rules
3) test coldmodel latency for customer SLAs
4) add alert for prefill token spike (threshold 50k tokens)

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2, customer-impact=true, status=mitigated (partial).

support-ops: Sent second customer update: \"Mitigations are in place and error rates are declining. We're actively monitoring and will reach out with a complete post-incident summary.\" :thumbsup:

maria-sre: I'll keep the runtime config on spill_to_disk=true for next 2 hours and watch for regressions.

oncall: Handoff in 30m -> @jordan. Checklist for handoff included in incident ticket.

jordan: ack, taking handoff at 18:10 UTC. Will verify:
- restarts stopped
- fallback working for >32k token cases
- customer follow-up ticket assigned
- assign postmortem owner

liam: Thanks team — please add any additional logs to the ticket. Postmortem owner: @maria-sre.

jordan: noted, will run a spike test against dedicated-gpu-pool-b to ensure it can sustain long-context load once traffic is shifted back.

incident-bot: Note: runbook link -> https://internal.runbooks/redwood/prefill-oom (added).

maria-sre: closing slack loop for now. Will reopen if OOMs resurge.
